title: Abstract 2-SAT dimer instance for state-change design
description: An abstract 2-SAT formula encoded as a dimer patchy-particle system. This problem contains the logical structure (two conditions) that must be satisfied through state-changing patchy particles.

sat_instance.convention: Two independent conditions: B (TF) and D (TT). Each condition is a 2-SAT clause where the first element is the condition name and the second is the truth table pattern (TF = True OR False, TT = True AND True).

condition_B.description: Allows only 1 false (A) monomer to be attached at a time. If A,A are attached simultaneously to B on both faces, one (higher ID) flips to C (true). If C,C or A,C are attached, nothing happens.

monomers.B: condition monomer with two patch faces (B_face1, B_face2)

condition_D.description: Both need to be true (F). If even one false (E) attaches to D, it switches to type F (true).

monomers.D: condition monomer with two patch faces (D_face1, D_face2)

problem_structure.independence: The two sets A,B,C and D,E,F are independent and do not interact with each other.
problem_structure.solution: If we set B to True (ON), both rules are satisfied: (Anything ∨ True) = True for both conditions.

simulation_constraints.notes: Competitors must design a dimer system with two independent channels (A,B,C and D,E,F) following the state-change logic described above. Use the same structure and potentials as the basic competition (see state-change/dimer_ksat/twosideB_twin).

expected_decode.measurement: Solution is measured by the concentration of true/false particles at the end of the simulation. B=True satisfies both conditions.
expected_decode.tolerance: The decoded assignment must satisfy both conditions. We will verify independently.

scoring.description: Higher concentration of true particles (C and F) at the end of simulation is better. The solution B=True should maximize this.
